headline: Masatsu is a Middle Chinese compound, 摩擦 (MC ma tshat).
Bushu, “radical”, is from Middle Chinese 部首, first mentioned in Chinese in the Shūowén Jiězì of roughly 100 CE.
Arai is cognate with 粗い (arai).
Fukuramu, “to swell”, is 膨 (fukura, “a bulge, a swelling”) plus -mu, first cited to the mid-800s.
Massaki is 真っ (ma'-, “truly”) plus 先 (saki, “first”).
Ji, “character”, is from Middle Chinese 字.
Sakeru is from 避く (saku), cognate with 裂ける (sakeru).
Kō, “this way”, shifted from 斯く (kaku): kaku, kau, kɔː, then kō.
Aruiwa is ある (aru, “to be, to exist”) plus a nominalizing い plus は (wa, topic marker), and arose from 漢文訓読.
Suu, “to suck”, is likely an onomatopoeia; the page compares words from Middle Korean to Proto-Indo-European.
Senshū, “last week”, is first attested in the 1920s.
Tomaru, “to stay overnight”, is a doublet of 止まる (tomaru).
Kai, “shell”, was kapi in Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *kapi.
Toriageru is 取る (toru, “to take”) plus 上げる (ageru, “to raise, lift”).
Doku, “poison”, is from Middle Chinese 毒.
Minna is a shift from みな (mina), with a doubled consonant added.
Kitai is Sinitic 氣體 (qìtǐ).
Jinsei is from Middle Chinese 人生.
Junjo is 順 (jun, “order”) plus 序 (jo, “order”): “order” twice.
Nemuru shifted from neburu, from the same root as Old Japanese 寝 (nu), which gives 寝る (neru).
Meijiru shifted from 命ずる (meizuru), as an s-irregular verb ending in -uru became an upper monograde verb in -iru.
Hontō first appears in a text of 1770, and the clipped honto first appears in 1886.
Shiokarai is 塩 (shio, “salt”) plus 辛い (karai, “harsh (of flavor); spicy, salty”).
Akiru comes from earlier 飽く (aku), irregularly evolved to the kami ichidan conjugation.
Kazoeru began as kazu apu, and took six steps to reach kazoeru.
Shōkyokuteki is 消極 (shōkyoku) plus 的 (-teki).
Kore is from Old Japanese; compare Okinawan くり (kuri).
Kuzureru comes from Old Japanese 崩る (kuduru).
Anketo is borrowed from French enquête, “inquest”.
Tsure is the continuative stem of 連れる (tsureru, “to accompany, lead”).
Shū, “state”, is from Middle Chinese 州, and 州 is a daiyōji replacing 洲.
